The patient is an 8-year-old girl with a history of acute sinusitis treated with amoxicillin, presenting with low-grade fever, itchy rash (wheals/hives), and generalized joint pain. The rash started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae and spread to the trunk and distal extremities. There is no history of adverse drug reactions, and immunizations are up to date. There is no significant joint swelling, change in urine output, angioedema, or respiratory distress.

The clinical presentation of fever, rash, and arthralgia following antibiotic use (amoxicillin) is highly suggestive of a serum sickness-like reaction (SSLR). SSLR is a type III hypersensitivity reaction that typically occurs 1-2 weeks after exposure to the offending agent (often penicillins or cephalosporins).
